newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk Celik Halat to meet 1997 targets.
newsitem.headline: Turk Celik Halat to meet 1997 targets.

text.p: Turkey's leading steel wire and rope producer Celik Halat ve Tel Sanayii A.S. will meet its $38-million turnover target in 1997, a senior company official said.

"The results of the first half of 1997 and bursting orders for the rest of the year show that we will meet our $38-million, or six trillion lira, turnover target this year," said Selami Kaplan, general manager of the company.
"This result will lead to a one trillion profit," he told Reuters in an interview.
Celik Halat reported total sales of 2.9 trillion lira and 561 billion lira pre-tax profit in 1996.
Share prices of the company opened at 4,400 lira on Thursday on the Istanbul Stock Exchange, up from Wednesday's close of 4,350 lira.
The company aims to increase its total sales to $46 million in 1998, $55 million in 1999 and $70 million in 2000.
Kaplan said nearly half of its total sales in 1996 came from exports, which totalled $20 million last year.
The share of exports in total sales were 44 percent in June this year, up from 30 percent at the end of the first three months. The end-year target for the figure is 50 percent.
Celik Halat completed a capacity expansion investment in May and increased the annual production capacity to 53,000 tonnes from 38,000 tonnes with a $3 million spending.
Kaplan said they aimed to increase total production to 41,300 tonnes this year from 36,000 tonnes in 1996.
"New lines became operational in June and they will affect the production figures for the rest of the year," he said.
"We will reach the 53,000 tonnes production next year with 100 percent capacity utilisation, which stands at 85 percent currently," he added.
The company will use $2 million, which it obtained from the government in benefits from an incentive package, for a plan to boost productivity, he said.
Celik Halat is the only integrated steel wire and rope producer in Turkey and controls approximately 64 percent of the domestic market.
The company has a large product variety with 8,000 types, including galvanized steel wire and ropes, strands, tire bead wires and concrete wires.
"The rest of the market is controlled by East European and Chinese products and some domestic small-scale companies," Kaplan said.
Celik Halat imports all its raw material from Britain, Italy, Spain and some other European and far-east countries.
The company reported 267 billion lira net profit in the first-half of this year against 158 billion lira in the same period of last year.
